adds.title: LGBTQ rights in the Philippines - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's national overview supplies the framework a visitor to the Zamboanga Peninsula stands under: non-commercial, private, consensual same-sex activity is legal in the Philippines, but transgender people cannot change their legal gender, the Family Code defines marriage as between a man and a woman, and there is no national anti-discrimination law covering sexual orientation or gender identity (only an anti-bullying law in basic education and a still-pending SOGIE Equality Bill). The page's local-ordinance section names Zamboanga City - the peninsula's regional center - among the 20+ local governments with their own anti-discrimination ordinances, listing Zamboanga City's as enacted in 2020 (cited to a Daily Tribune report of 28 December 2020), so the local legal floor in the region includes this SOGIE protection.

adds.title: LGBTQ rights in the Philippines - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's national framework page sets out what applies across the Bicol Region: consensual same-sex activity is legal, transgender people may not change their legal gender, the Family Code confines marriage to a man and a woman, and no national anti-discrimination statute exists (only an anti-bullying law covering SOGIE in basic education and the pending SOGIE Equality Bill). For the region itself the page records that Albay province - entirely within Bicol - enacted a province-wide sexual-orientation and gender-identity anti-discrimination ordinance in 2022, one of nine provinces with such protection, and it lists the Gayon Albay LGBT Organization, described as 'predominantly active in the Bicol region', among established local groups.
